questions.question: What is the study of rocks called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Petrology**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Petrology**

 
 
• Petrology is the scientific study of rocks, encompassing their origin, composition, texture, and structure.
 
• It delves into the processes that form and transform rocks, such as igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary processes.
 
• Petrologists investigate the mineral composition of rocks, their physical properties, and the geological conditions under which they formed.
 
• This field plays a crucial role in understanding the Earth's history and the dynamics of geological processes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fruit Science (Pomology)**

 
 
• Pomology is the branch of horticulture that focuses on the cultivation, breeding, and study of fruits.
 
• It encompasses various aspects of fruit production, including tree and vine training, fruit quality assessment, disease and pest management, and the development of new fruit varieties.
 
• Pomology contributes to improving fruit production, enhancing fruit quality, and ensuring sustainable fruit cultivation practices.
 
 
 
• **Mycology**
 
 
• Mycology is the scientific study of fungi.
 
• It explores the biology, genetics, biochemistry, taxonomy, and ecology of fungi, which include yeasts, molds, and mushrooms.
 
• Mycology has significant implications in various fields, including medicine (antibiotics, immunology), agriculture (mycorrhizae, biocontrol agents), and industry (food production, bioremediation).
 
 
 
• **Soil Science (Pedology)**
 
 
• Soil science is the study of soil, its formation, properties, classification, and management.
 
• It investigates soil composition (minerals, organic matter), soil structure, soil water, soil fertility, and the impact of human activities on soil quality.
 
• Soil science is crucial for sustainable agriculture, environmental protection, and understanding the Earth's ecosystems.

questions.question: According to the UNDP Human Development Report 2021-22, what was the Human Development Index rank of India?

The correct answer is __**132**__.

__
 
• The Human Development Report 2021-22 provides comprehensive data on various aspects of human development, including poverty.
 
• According to the report, 8.8% of the population in India is under severe multi-dimensional poverty.
 
• Multi-dimensional poverty considers various factors beyond income, such as health, education, and living standards.
 
• This statistic highlights the challenges faced by a significant portion of the population in accessing basic services and opportunities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Human Development Report (HDR)

 
 
• The HDR is an annual report published by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• It focuses on key dimensions of human development: a long and healthy life, access to knowledge, and a decent standard of living.
 
• The report includes the Human Development Index (HDI), which ranks countries based on these dimensions.
 
• The HDR also addresses pressing global issues, such as inequality, gender disparity, and environmental sustainability.
 
 
 
• Multi-dimensional Poverty Index (MPI)
 
 
• The MPI is a measure developed by the UNDP and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI).
 
• It assesses the multiple deprivations that people face in health, education, and living standards.
 
• Indicators include nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, school attendance, cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, and assets.
 
• Individuals are considered multi-dimensionally poor if they are deprived in at least one-third of the weighted indicators.
 
 
 
• Severe Multi-dimensional Poverty
 
 
• This term refers to individuals who are deprived in at least half of the weighted indicators of the MPI.
 
• It highlights extreme levels of deprivation across multiple dimensions, exacerbating the challenges of overcoming poverty.
 
• Addressing severe multi-dimensional poverty requires comprehensive policies that target health, education, and living standards simultaneously.

questions.question: Originally, the Constitution of India had ________ Schedules.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Constitution of India:

 
 
• The Constitution of India is the supreme law of the land, laying down the framework that defines the political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
 
 
• Schedules in the Constitution:
 
 
• The Constitution originally had 8 schedules, but now it has 12 schedules. These schedules are lists in the Constitution that categorize and tabulate bureaucratic activity and government policy.
 
 
 
• Details of the 12 Schedules:
 
 
• First Schedule: Lists the states and territories of India.
 
• Second Schedule: Provisions related to the President, Governors, Judges, and Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
 
• Third Schedule: Forms of Oaths or Affirmations.
 
• Fourth Schedule: Allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha.
 
• Fifth Schedule: Provisions related to the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.
 
• Sixth Schedule: Provisions for the administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.
 
• Seventh Schedule: Division of powers between the Union and States (Union List, State List, and Concurrent List).
 
• Eighth Schedule: Lists the official languages recognized by the Constitution.
 
• Ninth Schedule: Contains acts and laws that are exempt from judicial review.
 
• Tenth Schedule: Provisions related to disqualification of members on the ground of defection.
 
• Eleventh Schedule: Specifies the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Panchayats.
 
• Twelfth Schedule: Specifies the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Municipalities.

questions.question: In which year was the Bahmani Empire established?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1347 AD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bahmani Empire was established in **1347 AD** by **Ala-ud-Din Bahman Shah**.
 
• This empire was located in the **Deccan region** of South India, with its initial capital at Gulbarga and later at Bidar.
 
• The foundation of the Bahmani Empire marked the beginning of a long period of Muslim rule in the Deccan.
 
• The Bahmani rulers were known for their significant contributions to the **art, architecture, and culture** of the Deccan region.
 
• The kingdom was one of the major Muslim states in India and played a crucial role in the political and cultural history of the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deccan Sultanates**

 
 
• The Bahmani Empire eventually fragmented into five Deccan Sultanates: Bijapur, Golkonda, Ahmadnagar, Bidar, and Berar.
 
• These sultanates were prominent in the 16th and 17th centuries and were known for their contributions to Indo-Islamic culture and architecture.
 
• They played a significant role in the resistance against the Mughal expansion in the Deccan.
 
 
 
• **Ala-ud-Din Bahman Shah**
 
 
• The founder of the Bahmani Empire, originally known as Zafar Khan, was a former governor under the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• He declared independence from the Delhi Sultanate and established the Bahmani kingdom.
 
• His reign marked the beginning of the Bahmani dynasty, which ruled the Deccan for nearly two centuries.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Contributions**
 
 
• The Bahmani rulers were great patrons of architecture, contributing to the development of Indo-Islamic architecture in the Deccan.
 
• Notable structures include the Jama Masjid in Gulbarga, the Gol Gumbaz in Bijapur, and the Bidar Fort.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Cultural Developments**
 
 
• The Bahmani Empire facilitated trade and cultural exchanges between the Deccan and other parts of the world, including Persia, Arabia, and Africa.
 
• The Bahmani court was known for its cosmopolitan culture, which included scholars, poets, and artists from different regions.

questions.question: Bharti Vitthal is primarily an award winning ________ dancer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bharti Vitthal is a renowned Indian classical dancer primarily known for her expertise in **Kuchipudi**.
 
• Kuchipudi is one of the major Indian classical dance forms originating from the state of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Bharti Vitthal has received numerous awards and accolades for her significant contributions to the art form.
 
• Her performances are celebrated for their grace, precision, and adherence to traditional Kuchipudi techniques.
 
• She has played a pivotal role in promoting and preserving the cultural heritage of Kuchipudi dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kuchipudi**

 
 
• Kuchipudi is a classical Indian dance form that combines fast rhythms, fluid movements, and dramatic expressions.
 
• The dance form is named after the village of Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh where it originated.
 
• It traditionally involves both solo and group performances, often depicting stories from Hindu mythology.
 
• Kuchipudi is known for its unique style of using a brass plate, where dancers perform intricate footwork while balancing on the edges of the plate.
 
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam is a major classical dance form originating from Tamil Nadu, known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate hand gestures.
 
• It is often accompanied by classical Carnatic music and emphasizes expressions and rhythmic dance movements.
 
• This dance form is traditionally performed by solo dancers.
 
 
 
• **Mohiniyattam**
 
 
• Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form from Kerala, characterized by graceful and swaying movements.
 
• The term "Mohiniyattam" comes from "Mohini," a mythical enchantress avatar of Vishnu, and "attam," meaning dance.
 
• It is performed by women and is known for its elegant and soft movements.
 
 
 
• **Kathakali**
 
 
• Kathakali is a classical dance-drama form from Kerala, known for its elaborate costumes, makeup, and masks.
 
• It combines dance, music, acting, and ritualistic elements to present stories from epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana.
 
• Performers use detailed gestures, facial expressions, and body movements to convey the story and emotions.

questions.question: The flagship programme of the Government of India, 'Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan' fulfills which of the following provisions of the Directive Principles of State Policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 45**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 45** of the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution mandates the state to provide free and compulsory education for all children until they complete the age of fourteen years.
 
• **Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA)** was launched in 2001 to fulfil this mandate by ensuring universal access to education.
 
• The SSA aims to improve human capabilities through provision of community-owned quality education in a mission mode.
 
• The programme also seeks to bridge social, regional, and gender gaps, with the active participation of the community in the management of schools.
 
• The Right to Education Act (RTE) 2009 further strengthens Article 45 by making education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**

 
 
• DPSPs are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government, which are non-justiciable in nature.
 
• These principles aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They are enumerated in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, from Articles 36 to 51.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009**
 
 
• It provides for free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years in India.
 
• It mandates that no child shall be held back, expelled, or required to pass a board examination until the completion of elementary education.
 
• The act also stipulates that the child or his/her parents shall not be subject to any screening procedure for admission to a school.
 
 
 
• **Universalization of Elementary Education**
 
 
• It refers to making education accessible to all children of elementary school age.
 
• SSA and RTE are significant steps towards achieving this goal in India.
 
 
 
• **Community Participation in Education**
 
 
• Involvement of local communities in the management and administration of schools.
 
• Encourages accountability and ensures that the educational needs of the community are met.

questions.question: Which of the following ministries established the National Skill Development Corporation?

options.text: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

__
 
• The National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) was established by the Ministry of Finance.
 
• NSDC is a not-for-profit public limited company.
 
• It was set up by the Ministry of Finance in 2008 under Section 25 of the Companies Act, 1956 (now Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013).
 
• The NSDC aims to promote skill development by catalyzing the creation of large, quality, for-profit vocational institutions.
 
• It also provides funding to build scalable and profitable vocational training initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It oversees several programs like the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) and the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS).
 
• The Ministry aims to provide the institutional capacity to train, upskill, and reskill the workforce.
 
• MSDE also works closely with NSDC to implement its various skill development initiatives.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)**
 
 
• Launched in 2015, PMKVY is the flagship scheme of the MSDE.
 
• It aims to enable a large number of Indian youth to take up industry-relevant skill training to secure a better livelihood.
 
• The scheme is implemented through NSDC.
 
• Short-term training programs are provided to unemployed youth and school/college dropouts.
 
• Successful candidates receive skill certificates and placement assistance.
 
 
 
• **National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS)**
 
 
• NAPS was launched on August 19, 2016, to promote apprenticeship training and increase the engagement of apprentices.
 
• It provides financial support to establishments undertaking apprenticeship programs.
 
• The scheme is implemented by the Directorate General of Training (DGT) under MSDE.
 
• It aims to bridge the skill gap and enhance the employability of youth.

questions.question: What is the interaction of a species with all the biotic and abiotic factors affecting it called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ecological niche**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An **ecological niche** refers to the role and position a species has in its environment, including all the interactions with biotic and abiotic factors.
 
• It encompasses how a species meets its needs for food and shelter, how it survives, and how it reproduces.
 
• The concept of the ecological niche includes both the physical space an organism occupies and the ecological role it performs.
 
• It is a fundamental concept in ecology that helps in understanding how species coexist and interact within ecosystems.
 
• Understanding a species' ecological niche is crucial for conservation efforts and managing biodiversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biotic Factors:**

 
 
• Biotic factors are the living components of an ecosystem, such as plants, animals, and microorganisms.
 
• These factors influence the distribution and abundance of organisms within an ecosystem.
 
• Interactions among biotic factors include predation, competition, and symbiosis.
 
 
 
• **Abiotic Factors:**
 
 
• Abiotic factors are the non-living physical and chemical elements in the environment, such as sunlight, temperature, wind, and water.
 
• These factors significantly impact the survival and reproduction of organisms.
 
• They help shape the habitat and influence the ecological niche of a species.
 
 
 
• **Food Web:**
 
 
• A food web is a complex network of feeding relationships among different organisms in an ecosystem.
 
• It illustrates how energy and nutrients flow through ecological communities.
 
• Unlike food chains, food webs provide a more comprehensive depiction of how species interact and depend on one another for food.
 
 
 
• **Food Chain:**
 
 
• A food chain is a linear sequence of organisms through which nutrients and energy pass as one organism eats another.
 
• It typically starts with a primary producer (like plants) and moves up to primary consumers (herbivores) and secondary consumers (carnivores).
 
• Food chains are simpler and less interconnected compared to food webs.

questions.question: Which technique is used in cell biology research to image cellular organelles and surface topography?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Scanning electron microscopy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM)** is widely used to image the surface topography and detailed structure of cellular organelles.
 
• SEM provides high-resolution, three-dimensional images by scanning the specimen surface with a focused beam of electrons.
 
• The technique is crucial for studying the morphology and composition of biological samples at nanoscale levels.
 
• SEM's ability to provide detailed images of the cell surface makes it indispensable in cell biology research and material sciences.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phase Contrast Microscopy:**

 
 
• A technique that enhances contrast in transparent and colorless specimens, making it useful for live cell imaging.
 
• It works by converting phase shifts in light passing through a specimen to brightness changes in the image.
 
 
 
• **Fluorescence Microscopy:**
 
 
• Used to study properties of organic or inorganic substances using fluorescence instead of, or in addition to, reflection and absorption.
 
• It is vital for imaging specific structures within cells using fluorescent dyes or proteins.
 
 
 
• **Dark-field Microscopy:**
 
 
• A technique that enhances contrast in unstained specimens, useful for viewing live and transparent specimens.
 
• It works by blocking direct light and collecting only scattered light to form an image.
 
 
 
• **Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM):**
 
 
• A technique that provides detailed images of the internal structure of thinly sliced specimens.
 
• It uses a beam of electrons transmitted through the specimen to form an image.

• The **101st Constitutional Amendment Act** of 2016 introduced the provision for the establishment of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council.
 
• The GST Council was constituted on **12th September 2016**.
 
• The Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and includes the Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance and the Ministers in charge of Finance or Taxation or any other Minister nominated by each state government.
 
• The GST Council makes recommendations to the Union and the States on important issues related to GST, such as the goods and services that may be subjected to or exempted from GST, model GST laws, principles of levy, apportionment of GST, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Amendment**

 
 
• A constitutional amendment is a modification of the constitution of a nation or a state.
 
• In India, constitutional amendments are made by Parliament and require a special majority.
 
 
 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**
 
 
• GST is a comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based tax that is levied on every value addition.
 
• It is a single tax on the supply of goods and services, right from the manufacturer to the consumer.
 
• Credits of input taxes paid at each stage are available in the subsequent stage of value addition, which makes GST essentially a tax only on value addition at each stage.
 
 
 
• **GST Council**
 
 
• The GST Council is a constitutional body for making recommendations to the Union and State Governments on issues related to Goods and Service Tax.
 
• The Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
 
• It ensures that the tax system is uniform across the country and avoids the cascading of taxes.
 
 
 
• **Implementation of GST**
 
 
• GST was implemented in India on 1st July 2017.
 
• It subsumed various indirect taxes like VAT, service tax, excise duty, etc.
 
• GST aims to simplify the tax structure, increase compliance, and broaden the tax base.

questions.question: What do you understand by 'barter system'?

options.text: purchase of goods in exchange for money
purchase and sale of goods for goods
sale of goods in exchange for money

questions.solution:

__
 
• The barter system is a method of trade where goods and services are exchanged directly for other goods and services without the use of money.
 
• This system relies on the double coincidence of wants, meaning both parties must have what the other desires.
 
• Barter systems were prevalent in ancient civilizations before the advent of money.
 
• It is still used in some communities and in situations where currency is unstable or unavailable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Double Coincidence of Wants:**

 
 
• This is a situation where two parties each possess an item the other wants, facilitating an exchange.
 
• It is a fundamental challenge in a barter system as it requires finding a matching need.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Barter:**
 
 
• Barter systems can be inefficient, especially with complex needs and large societies.
 
• The lack of a common measure of value can complicate transactions.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Bartering dates back to 6000 BC, introduced by Mesopotamian tribes and adopted by Phoenicians.
 
• Various items such as salt, spices, and weapons were commonly exchanged.
 
 
 
• **Modern Use:**
 
 
• Barter still exists in modern economies during times of monetary crisis.
 
• Some businesses use barter networks or exchanges to trade excess inventory for needed goods.

questions.question: The aim of the Permanent Settlement Act of 1793 was to enter into an agreement for fixed revenue collection between the East India Company and _________.

__
 
• The Permanent Settlement Act of 1793 was introduced by the British East India Company under the leadership of Lord Cornwallis.
 
• This act aimed to create a fixed revenue system by entering into agreements with landlords (Zamindars) for revenue collection.
 
• The landlords were responsible for collecting taxes from the peasants and paying a fixed amount to the Company.
 
• It was intended to stabilize revenue collection and ensure a steady income for the British administration.
 
• Landlords were given hereditary rights over the land, which they could pass on to their descendants.

• **Zamindari System**

• Under this system, Zamindars were recognized as landowners by the British government.
 
• The system aimed to create a class of loyal landlords who would support British rule.
 
 
 
• **Revenue Settlement**
 
 
• Revenue Settlement refers to the agreement made between the British government and landlords for tax collection.
 
• It ensured that the government received a fixed amount of revenue annually.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Peasants**
 
 
• Peasants were often exploited as landlords sought to maximize revenue collection.
 
• Many peasants faced high taxes and were at risk of losing their land.
 
 
 
• **Permanent Settlement Act**
 
 
• The act was part of the larger framework of British colonial administration in India.
 
• It laid the foundation for the modern land revenue system in Bengal and later extended to other parts of India.

• **Starch detection:** Iodine test is used to detect the presence of starch in food items. The iodine solution turns blue-black in the presence of starch.
 
• **Fat detection:** Acrolein test is used for the detection of fats in food items. This test involves heating the fat and detecting the acrolein formed, which has a pungent odor.

questions.question: For how many months can a person be appointed as Chief Minister without being a member of the State Legislature?

__
 
• According to the Constitution of India, a person who is not a member of the state legislature can be appointed as the Chief Minister.
 
• However, such a person must get elected to the state legislature within six months from the date of their appointment.
 
• This provision ensures that the Chief Minister has the confidence of the legislature.
 
• If the person fails to get elected within the stipulated six-month period, they must step down from the position of Chief Minister.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 164(4) of the Indian Constitution**

 
 
• This article specifies the provision for a non-legislator to be appointed as a Minister, including the Chief Minister.
 
• It mandates that such an individual must become a member of the state legislature within six months.
 
 
 
• **Role of Chief Minister**
 
 
• The Chief Minister is the head of the government at the state level.
 
• They are responsible for the administration of the state and the implementation of state policies.
 
 
 
• **State Legislature**
 
 
• The state legislature consists of the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) and, in some states, the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad).
 
• Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs) are directly elected by the people.
 
 
 
• **Confidence of the House**
 
 
• It is essential for the Chief Minister to have the majority support in the Legislative Assembly.
 
• This support is crucial for the stability of the state government.

questions.question: The Brahmo Samaj was founded in 1828 by who among the following social reformers of British India?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Brahmo Samaj was founded by **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** in 1828.
 
• It was established in Kolkata, India.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj aimed at reforming the religious and social practices of the Hindus.
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy is often called the **‘Father of the Indian Renaissance’** for his efforts in social and religious reform.
 
• The organization played a key role in the movement against **practices like Sati** and child marriage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmo Samaj**

 
 
• It is a monotheistic reform movement within Hinduism.
 
• The organization was against idol worship and aimed to restore the Hindu faith to its original purity.
 
• It advocated for the brotherhood of all religions and the worship of one God.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj also worked towards improving women's rights and education.
 
 
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**
 
 
• He was a prominent Indian social reformer and the founder of the Brahmo Samaj.
 
• He is known for his efforts to abolish the practice of Sati.
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy is also credited with advocating for the modern education system in India.
 
• He was a proponent of free speech and the press.
 
 
 
• **Sati**
 
 
• Sati was a historical Hindu funeral practice where a widow self-immolated on her husband's pyre.
 
• The practice was abolished in 1829 due to the efforts of Raja Ram Mohan Roy and the British government.
 
• The regulation prohibiting Sati was signed by Governor-General Lord William Bentinck.
 
 
 
• **Social Reform Movements in India**
 
 
• The 19th century saw several social reform movements aimed at eradicating social evils.
 
• Key figures included Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, and Jyotirao Phule.
 
• These movements focused on issues like women's education, abolition of child marriage, and the upliftment of marginalized communities.
 
• They played a significant role in shaping modern Indian society.

questions.question: The power to create _________ lies only with the Legislative Assembly.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Money Bill**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Legislative Assembly, not in the Legislative Council, as per Article 198 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Money Bills deal with matters like imposition, abolition, remission, alteration, or regulation of any tax.
 
• They also cover the borrowing of money by the government, the custody of the Consolidated Fund or Contingency Fund of India, and the appropriation of money out of these funds.
 
• The Legislative Assembly has the exclusive power to introduce and pass Money Bills, while the Legislative Council can only suggest amendments, which the Assembly may or may not accept.
 
• A Money Bill is defined under Article 110 of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 110 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• Defines what constitutes a Money Bill in the Indian legal framework.
 
• Specifies that a Bill is considered a Money Bill if it deals exclusively with matters specified in Article 110 (1).
 
 
 
• **Role of the Legislative Council:**
 
 
• The Legislative Council has limited powers in the case of a Money Bill, as it can only make recommendations within 14 days.
 
• It cannot amend or reject a Money Bill; the final decision rests with the Legislative Assembly.
 
 
 
• **Consolidated Fund of India:**
 
 
• It comprises all revenues received by the government, loans raised by it, and money received in repayment of loans.
 
• All government expenditures are made from this fund, subject to authorization by the legislature.
 
 
 
• **Financial Bill:**
 
 
• A Financial Bill also contains provisions related to revenue or expenditure but is different from a Money Bill as it can be introduced in either House of Parliament.
 
• Unlike a Money Bill, it does not exclusively deal with matters listed in Article 110.

questions.question: Which is the largest component of GDP?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Consumption**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Consumption** is the largest component of GDP in most economies, accounting for approximately 60-70% of total GDP.
 
• It includes all private expenditures by households and non-profit institutions serving households on goods and services.
 
• Consumption expenditures are divided into durable goods (e.g., cars, appliances), non-durable goods (e.g., food, clothing), and services (e.g., healthcare, education).
 
• This component reflects the overall spending behavior and economic activity of individuals and households within an economy.
 
• Changes in consumption patterns can significantly impact economic growth and stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**

 
 
• GDP is the total monetary value of all finished goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period.
 
• It is a comprehensive measure of a nation's overall economic activity and an indicator of economic health.
 
• GDP can be calculated using three approaches: production (or output), income, and expenditure.
 
• Real GDP is adjusted for inflation, while nominal GDP is not.
 
 
 
• **Investment**
 
 
• Investment, also known as gross fixed capital formation, includes business expenditures on capital goods such as buildings, machinery, and equipment.
 
• It is essential for long-term economic growth and productivity improvements.
 
• Investment typically accounts for 15-20% of GDP.
 
 
 
• **Government Purchases**
 
 
• This component includes all government consumption expenditures and gross investment.
 
• It covers spending on defense, education, public safety, and infrastructure.
 
• Government purchases usually account for 15-20% of GDP.
 
 
 
• **Net Exports**
 
 
• Net exports are calculated as the difference between a country's exports and imports of goods and services.
 
• A positive net export indicates a trade surplus, while a negative net export indicates a trade deficit.
 
• Net exports can significantly affect GDP but often constitute a smaller share compared to other components.

questions.question: Green Revolution was mainly for which crops?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India primarily focused on the cultivation of **wheat and rice**.
 
• It began in the 1960s with the introduction of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds.
 
• Norman Borlaug, an American agronomist, is often credited with the development and spread of these high-yielding wheat seeds.
 
• MS Swaminathan played a key role in bringing the Green Revolution to India, making the country self-sufficient in food grains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High-Yielding Varieties (HYV)**

 
 
• These are seeds developed to increase the productivity of crops.
 
• HYV seeds are often resistant to diseases and pests.
 
• They require more water and fertilizers compared to traditional seeds.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Farmers**
 
 
• The Green Revolution increased the income of farmers who adopted HYV seeds.
 
• It led to regional disparities, benefiting mainly the Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh regions.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Concerns**
 
 
• Excessive use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides has led to soil degradation.
 
• Overuse of water resources for irrigation has resulted in water scarcity in some areas.
 
 
 
• **Food Security**
 
 
• The Green Revolution played a crucial role in making India self-sufficient in food grains.
 
• It helped in reducing India's dependence on food imports.

questions.question: In terms of precipitation patterns, what does Cf mean in warm temperate climates?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Precipitation throughout the year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Cf** denotes a climate classification within the Köppen system where 'C' stands for warm temperate climates and 'f' indicates a lack of dry season.
 
• In a Cf climate, precipitation is distributed **evenly throughout the year**.
 
• Such climates are typically found in regions with **moderate to high annual rainfall**, without a significant dry period.
 
• Examples of Cf climates include **Western Europe** and parts of the eastern United States.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Köppen Climate Classification**

 
 
• Developed by Wladimir Köppen, it categorizes the world’s climates based on **temperature and precipitation patterns**.
 
• The system uses a combination of letters to describe the major climate types and subtypes.
 
• The primary categories include Tropical (A), Dry (B), Temperate (C), Continental (D), and Polar (E).
 
 
 
• **Warm Temperate Climates (C)**
 
 
• These climates are characterized by **mild winters** and warm or hot summers.
 
• Commonly found in **mid-latitude regions** of the world.
 
• Subdivisions include Mediterranean (Cs), Humid Subtropical (Cfa), and Oceanic (Cfb).
 
 
 
• **Humid Subtropical Climate (Cfa)**
 
 
• Characterized by hot, humid summers and mild winters.
 
• Commonly found in southeastern parts of the United States, eastern China, and parts of South America.
 
• Receives abundant rainfall throughout the year, often with summer peak.
 
 
 
• **Oceanic Climate (Cfb)**
 
 
• Known for cool summers, mild winters, and **moderate year-round precipitation**.
 
• Predominantly found in **Western Europe** and parts of the Pacific Northwest.
 
• Influenced by proximity to oceans, leading to smaller temperature ranges.

__
 
• **D.P. Dhar** was the key figure behind the drafting and launching of the Fifth Five Year Plan in India.
 
• The Fifth Five Year Plan aimed at achieving **self-reliance and poverty alleviation**.
 
• This plan covered the period from **1974 to 1979**.
 
• D.P. Dhar was a prominent Indian diplomat and politician who played a significant role in economic planning during this period.
 
• The plan was eventually terminated prematurely in 1978 by the subsequent government led by Prime Minister Morarji Desai.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five Year Plans in India**

 
 
• These were centralized and integrated national economic programs.
 
• The concept was derived from the Soviet Union's planning system.
 
• The first Five Year Plan was launched in 1951, focusing on the agricultural sector.
 
• India has had a total of twelve Five Year Plans before the planning commission was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015.
 
 
 
• **D.P. Dhar**
 
 
• Dhar was an influential member of the Indian National Congress and closely associated with Indira Gandhi.
 
• He also served as the Indian Ambassador to the Soviet Union.
 
• His contributions were pivotal during the Indo-Pakistani War of 1971.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of the Fifth Five Year Plan**
 
 
• The plan targeted the reduction of poverty (Garibi Hatao) and attainment of self-reliance.
 
• It emphasized employment generation and equitable distribution of income.
 
• Special focus was on the development of the weaker sections of society.
 
 
 
• **Termination of the Fifth Five Year Plan**
 
 
• The plan was terminated in 1978 by the Janata Party government.
 
• The government introduced a new plan called the Rolling Plan.
 
• The Rolling Plan system was short-lived and was replaced by the Sixth Five Year Plan.

questions.question: Shakoor Khan is associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarangi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Shakoor Khan comes from a distinguished lineage of Sarangi players, contributing significantly to the preservation of this classical instrument.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarangi:**

 
 
• The Sarangi is a traditional string instrument used in Hindustani classical music.
 
• It is known for its deep, resonant sound and is considered one of the most difficult Indian instruments to master.
 
• The instrument is typically made from a single block of wood, with three main playing strings and around thirty-five sympathetic strings.
 
• Sarangi players use a bow to play, and it is held vertically on the lap while playing.
 
 
 
• **Hindustani Classical Music:**
 
 
• It is a tradition of Indian classical music that originated in North India.
 
• Hindustani classical music has a rich history and encompasses a variety of vocal and instrumental forms.
 
• It is typically based on ragas (melodic frameworks) and talas (rhythmic cycles).
 
• Instruments commonly used include the sitar, tabla, sarangi, and harmonium.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Music:**
 
 
• Indian classical music is broadly divided into two major traditions: Hindustani (North Indian) and Carnatic (South Indian).
 
• It has a complex and rich history, deeply rooted in ancient texts and traditions.
 
• Indian classical music is characterized by its extensive use of improvisation within the framework of a raga and tala.
 
• It plays a crucial role in Indian culture and has a profound spiritual and emotional impact on its listeners.
 
 
 
• **Musical Lineages in India:**
 
 
• India has a rich tradition of musical lineages or gharanas, which pass down musical knowledge and skills through generations.
 
• Each gharana has its unique style, techniques, and repertoire.
 
• Famous gharanas include the Maihar Gharana, Kirana Gharana, and Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana.
 
• These lineages play a vital role in preserving and propagating classical music traditions in India.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the Aligarh Muslim University in 1875?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Syed Ahmed Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Syed Ahmed Khan founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in 1875, which later became the Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.
 
• He was a prominent educator, Islamic reformer, and politician during the British Raj in India.
 
• His aim was to promote modern education among Muslims in India and to bridge the gap between the British and Indian Muslims.
 
• Syed Ahmed Khan is often credited with laying the foundation for the modern education system for Muslims in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aligarh Movement**

 
 
• The Aligarh Movement, started by Syed Ahmed Khan, aimed at reforming the social, educational, and political aspects of Muslim society in India.
 
• It emphasized the importance of modern education and scientific knowledge.
 
• The movement led to the establishment of several educational institutions and the promotion of Western-style education among Indian Muslims.
 
 
 
• **Syed Ahmed Khan's Contributions**
 
 
• He was a strong advocate for the adoption of Western education among Muslims.
 
• He founded several schools and colleges, including the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College.
 
• He wrote extensively on various subjects, including education, religion, and social issues.
 
• He was knighted by the British government in 1888 for his services to education and social reform.
 
 
 
• **Aligarh Muslim University**
 
 
• Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) is one of the oldest and most prestigious educational institutions in India.
 
• It offers a wide range of undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programs in various fields of study.
 
• AMU has played a significant role in the development of modern education and research in India.
 
• The university has a diverse student body and is known for its inclusive and secular environment.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is celebrated by the Jain community in Pawapuri, Bihar to commemorate the attainment of Nirvana by Lord Mahavira?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dev Deepawali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dev Deepawali is celebrated by the Jain community to honor the attainment of Nirvana by Lord Mahavira.
 
• This festival takes place in Pawapuri, Bihar, which is a significant pilgrimage site for Jains.
 
• Dev Deepawali is observed on the Kartik Purnima, which is the full moon day of the Hindu month of Kartik.
 
• The festival is marked by lighting lamps, offering prayers, and participating in various religious ceremonies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Mahavira**

 
 
• Lord Mahavira is the 24th Tirthankara in Jainism.
 
• He was born in 599 BCE in Bihar, India.
 
• Mahavira is known for his teachings on non-violence, truth, and asceticism.
 
• His teachings form the core of Jain philosophy and practice.
 
 
 
• **Pawapuri**
 
 
• Pawapuri is a holy site in Bihar, associated with Lord Mahavira's Nirvana.
 
• It is home to significant Jain temples like Jal Mandir and Samosharan Mandir.
 
• Jains from across the world visit Pawapuri during Dev Deepawali to pay their respects.
 
 
 
• **Kartik Purnima**
 
 
• Kartik Purnima is considered an auspicious day in Hindu, Sikh, and Jain traditions.
 
• It is celebrated with various religious activities, including lighting lamps and performing rituals.
 
• In Jainism, it holds special significance as the day of Lord Mahavira's Nirvana.

questions.question: Who among the following is a famous artist of Vilasini Natyam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swapnasundari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Swapnasundari** is a renowned Indian classical dancer and a celebrated artist of **Vilasini Natyam**.
 
• She has significantly contributed to the revival and popularization of Vilasini Natyam, a traditional dance form of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Vilasini Natyam is an ancient temple and court dance tradition that was once performed by temple dancers known as **Devadasis**.
 
• Swapnasundari has received numerous awards, including the prestigious **Padma Bhushan** for her contribution to Indian classical dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vilasini Natyam**

 
 
• It is a classical dance form originating from Andhra Pradesh, India.
 
• It was traditionally performed by female temple dancers, known as Devadasis, in temples and royal courts.
 
• The dance form integrates expressive storytelling through intricate hand gestures, facial expressions, and graceful body movements.
 
 
 
• **Swapnasundari's Contributions**
 
 
• She has worked extensively to revive and document Vilasini Natyam, ensuring its continuity and preservation.
 
• She has authored books and produced documentaries to educate and promote awareness about the dance form.
 
 
 
• **Devadasi Tradition**
 
 
• Devadasis were female artists dedicated to serving deities in temples, performing dance and music as a form of worship.
 
• This tradition faced decline during the colonial period due to socio-political changes and reform movements.
 
 
 
• **Padma Bhushan Award**
 
 
• The Padma Bhushan is the third-highest civilian award in India, recognizing distinguished service of a high order to the nation.
 
• It is awarded by the Government of India annually on Republic Day.
